verses.pali: saddhā, bhikkhave, upāsikā ekaputtakaṁ piyaṁ manāpaṁ evaṁ sammā āyācamānā āyāceyya:
verses.english: A faithful laywoman with a dear and beloved only son would rightly appeal to him,

verses.pali: ‘tādiso, tāta, bhavāhi yādiso citto ca gahapati hatthako ca āḷavako’ti.
verses.english: ‘My darling, please be like the householder Citta and Hatthaka of Āḷavī.’

verses.pali: Esā, bhikkhave, tulā etaṁ pamāṇaṁ mama sāvakānaṁ upāsakānaṁ, yadidaṁ citto ca gahapati hatthako ca āḷavako.
verses.english: These are a standard and a measure for my male lay disciples, that is, the householder Citta and Hatthaka of Āḷavī.

verses.pali: Sace kho tvaṁ, tāta, agārasmā anagāriyaṁ pabbajasi;
verses.english: ‘But my darling, if you go forth from the lay life to homelessness,
please be like Sāriputta and Moggallāna.’

verses.pali: Esā, bhikkhave, tulā etaṁ pamāṇaṁ mama sāvakānaṁ bhikkhūnaṁ, yadidaṁ sāriputtamoggalānā.
verses.english: These are a standard and a measure for my monk disciples, that is, Sāriputta and Moggallāna.

verses.pali: Mā ca kho tvaṁ, tāta, sekhaṁ appattamānasaṁ lābhasakkārasiloko anupāpuṇātūti.
verses.english: ‘And my darling, may you not come into possessions, honor, and popularity while you’re still a trainee and haven’t achieved your heart’s desire.’

verses.pali: Tañce, bhikkhave, bhikkhuṁ sekhaṁ appattamānasaṁ lābhasakkārasiloko anupāpuṇāti, so tassa hoti antarāyāya.
verses.english: If a trainee who hasn’t achieved their heart’s desire comes into possessions, honor, and popularity it’s an obstacle for them.
So grim are possessions, honor, and popularity. …”
